newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Gov. endorses $1.5 bln bridge plan -sources.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Gov. endorses $1.5 bln bridge plan -sources.

text.p: California Gov. Pete Wilson plans to endorse a more than $1.5-billion plan on Thursday that would replace the eastern span of the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge, administration sources said.
"The governor has made a decision based on public safety," one Wilson administration source said. "A new span would be the safest option available."

At a press briefing later Thursday, the Wilson administration is expected to back the $1.5 billion plan, which calls for the construction of a concrete bridge that would gradually rise from Oakland to Yerba Buena Island.

The $1.5 billion project would include the retrofit of the western section of the bridge. The project would likely receive bond funds already approved by voters in addition to revenues from higher bridge tolls.
Administration sources said Wilson would support a proposal to build a $1.7 billion cable stay bridge featuring two 650-foot towers, but only if San Francisco area residents agreed to the added cost.
State officials had been considering a plan to retrofit the entire bridge, but that $1.3 billion proposal was opposed by state seismic safety advisers.
